criteria_source: The fixture only. FINDINGS.md gives the query's predicate as date_trunc('day', created_at) = $1, records the ticket's proposal of a plain btree on the bare created_at column, and states in its own words that such an index cannot serve the query because the predicate compares the wrapped expression rather than the column. It supplies the two shapes that do work - an index on the date_trunc expression, which it notes must pass an explicit time zone to be IMMUTABLE, or a rewrite of the predicate to a half-open range on the bare column, after which a composite on tenant_id and created_at serves it. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This fixture is the expanded twin of the one in recall-index: it carries the same conclusion and the same qualification, and adds supporting material that is available to the answer but not required by the closed question. The added sections are the BUFFERS output and read-I/O share, a forced-index measurement, the verification that the proposed index was actually built and re-planned, measured build times and query times for both working shapes, the table's column layout and write pattern, four further ruled-out causes and rollout notes.
trap:
Passes when the answer denies that the proposed index on the bare created_at column fixes the query, and gives the fixture's reason: the predicate wraps created_at in date_trunc, so a btree on the raw column is not a candidate and the sequential scan stands. The answer must also point at a fix in one of the two families the fixture supplies - index the date_trunc expression itself, or rewrite the predicate to a half-open range on created_at so the bare-column index becomes usable. Either one is sufficient; naming both is not required. Fails when the answer confirms that the proposed index is the fix, when it agrees it will not work but gives a different reason - table size, bloat, the planner's cost estimate, the tenant_id index, connection pooling or the dashboard poll - or when it denies the index helps without offering either working shape. An answer that additionally notes the IMMUTABLE time-zone requirement on the expression index is still passing, since the fixture states it.

A response that asks which query or which table is meant, rather than reading FINDINGS.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
